intro: The Gambia is mainland Africa's smallest country, a thin strip of land along the Gambia River surrounded by Senegal.

chapters.title: River kingdoms
text: Mandinka, Wolof and Fula kingdoms lived along the river, which was part of the Mali Empire's trade network. The Wassu stone circles are over a thousand years old.

chapters.title: Kunta Kinteh Island
text: Europeans fought over a fort on James Island, now Kunta Kinteh Island, used in the slave trade. Britain made the Gambia a colony, and its odd shape follows the river, reaching about as far as British gunboats could sail.

highlight.title: Roots
highlight.text: Alex Haley's book Roots traced his ancestor Kunta Kinteh to the Gambian village of Juffureh.

chapters.title: Independence and democracy
text: The Gambia became independent in 1965. Yahya Jammeh ruled from a 1994 coup until 2017, when he lost an election and was forced to leave after regional pressure.

timeline.title: James Island fort
timeline.text: Built by Courland, a Baltic duchy.

keyTerms.meaning: A country almost surrounded by another.
